questions.q: Evaluate: $0.23\overline{472} + 0.24\overline{362}$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Direct Bar Expansion)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... fraction conversion mat lagana idhar, time waste ho jayega.

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction conversion $\frac{N}{99900}$ jaisi badsurat chize banati hain. Bar ko seedha expand kar ke add karna smartness hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
$0.23472472\dots$
$0.24362362\dots$
------------------
$0.47834834\dots$
Addition me $472 + 362 = 834$ sidha add ho raha hai bina kisi carry-forward (jo $>1000$ pe milta hai) ke. Iska matlab pattern perfectly $834$ ka hi banega.
Result = $0.47\overline{834}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Carry check hamesha right se aane wale cycle pe kiya karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Recurring decimals ko directly unki expanded form me likh ke basic addition karna sabse safe aur fast hai.

questions.q: Is zero considered an integer?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Bhai mere, Number system ki basic pehchan. Number line pe Zero bilkul center me baitha integer hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Integers ke 3 types hote hain:
1. Positive Integers ($+1, +2, +3\dots$)
2. Negative Integers ($-1, -2, -3\dots$)
3. Zero (Na positive, na negative).
Answer 'Yes' hai.

questions.q: Find the remainder when the polynomial $x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 5$ is divided by $x - 2$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Remainder theorem ka sabse direct hit hai. Divider ko zero rakho aur pen chalane ki zaroorat hi mat feel hone do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Divisor ko equals to zero maan kar seedha polynomial me $x=2$ phek de. Jo aayega wahi Remainder hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2 \\ (2)^3 - 3(2)^2 + 4(2) - 5 \\ 8 - 12 + 8 - 5 = -1 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Remainder Theorem state karta hai ki polynomial $P(x)$ ko jab linear divisor $x-a$ se divide karein to Remainder $P(a)$ hota hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 5 \\ R = P(2) \\ R = 8 - 12 + 8 - 5 = -1 $$

TCS Trap: Algebraic long division lagane ka try karega to wahan basic plus-minus mistakes hone ke 100% chances hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Divisor polynomial agar $ax-b$ form ka hai, toh Remainder is strictly equal to $P(b/a)$.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which when successively divided by $7$ and $8$ leaves remainders $2$ and $3$ respectively, and is a multiple of $5$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Number 'multiple of 5' hona chahiye, aur saare options multiples of 5 hain. Toh successive division se base equation bana lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, successive division ka standard equation bottom-up chalta hai. Let last quotient be $k$.
Number $N = 7(8k + 3) + 2 = 56k + 21 + 2 = 56k + 23$.
Ab is $N$ ko $5$ ka multiple ban na hai (yani aakhiri digit $0$ ya $5$ ho).
Agar main $k=0$ lu, $N = 23$ (Fail).
Agar main $k=1$ lu, $N = 79$ (Fail).
Agar main $k=2$ lu, $N = 112 + 23 = 135$. Ye pass ho gaya kyunki last me $5$ hai. Toh smallest answer $135$ hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
To solve $56k + 23 \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$, break it down: $(55k + k) + 20 + 3 \implies k + 3 \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$. Smallest positive integer $k$ satisfying this is $k=2$. Plugin $k=2$ in $56k+23$ gives $135$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division equation banakar Modulo reduction (Concept Builder method) is the most failsafe approach for CGL Mains.

questions.q: Find the number of factors of 14400 divisible by 18 but not by 36.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Combinatorics / Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... factors mein conditions set hain, iska matlab bas powers ko lock karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: $18 = 2^1 \times 3^2$ and $36 = 2^2 \times 3^2$. Difference sirf power of 2 ka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Prime factorize $14400 = 2^6 \times 3^2 \times 5^2$.
Divisible by $18$ matlab at least ($2^1 \times 3^2$) hona chahiye.
Not divisible by $36$ matlab ($2^2 \times 3^2$) nahi hona chahiye.
Requirement strict ho gayi: 2 ki power sirf $1$ ho sakti hai (1 choice). 3 ki power exactly $2$ rahegi kyunki max $3^2$ hi hai (1 choice). 5 ki power kuch bhi $0, 1, 2$ ho sakti hai (3 choices).
Combinations: $1 \times 1 \times 3 = 3$. Brilliant question!

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Divisible by X, not by Y' means lock the exact power of the prime that differs between X and Y.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of $31^{41^{51}}$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $31$

Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, base agar $1$ par end ho raha hai, toh seedha Aman Sir ka universal 'X1' wala jugad laagu hoga yahan.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Unit digit humesha $1$ hi rahegi. Tens digit ke liye, base ke tens ko power ke unit digit se multiply kar de. Khallas.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Base Tens} = 3 \\ \text{Power Unit} = 1 \text{ (Since } 41^{\text{anything}} \text{ ends in } 1) \\ \text{Result Tens} = 3 \times 1 = 3 \implies 31 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Binomial theorem se expand karne par baaki saari higher powers $100$ ka multiple ban jati hain, bas last do terms bach ti hain.

Mathematically :-

$$ (30+1)^k = \dots + k(30)(1) + 1 \\ \text{Last two digits} = (3k \pmod{10}) \times 10 + 1 $$

TCS Trap: Power ki actual power nikalne me bacha panic kar jata hai, jabki wahan sirf aakhiri digit hi matter karti hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> $(\dots x1)^y$ ke last two digits hamesha $(x \times \text{last digit of } y)$ and $1$ hote hain.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of $\frac{12^{55}}{3^{11}} + \frac{8^{48}}{16^{18}}$
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Never find unit digits before simplifying fractions! Denominators must be completely canceled out.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Term 1: $\frac{12^{55}}{3^{11}} = \frac{4^{55} \times 3^{55}}{3^{11}} = 4^{55} \times 3^{44}$.
Unit digit: $4^{\text{odd}} \implies 4$. $3^{44}$ (power is multiple of $4$) $\implies 1$. $4 \times 1 = 4$.
Term 2: $\frac{8^{48}}{16^{18}} = \frac{(2^3)^{48}}{(2^4)^{18}} = \frac{2^{144}}{2^{72}} = 2^{72}$.
Unit digit: $2^{72}$ (multiple of $4$) $\implies 6$.
Total Unit Digit = $4 + 6 = 10 \implies 0$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Indices ka base rule use kiya: $\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}$. Bacha denominator me fas ke galat unit digit nikalta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Simplification first, cyclicity second. Base same banao, powers minus karo.

questions.q: If a number is divided by a divisor D leaves remainder 17. If the number 3N is divided by D leaves a remainder 5. Find the remainder when 4N is divided by D?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Remainder Balancing)

Dekh bhai... Remainder theorem mein equations banayi toh phasega. Seedha operation remainders pe karna hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 3 times hua toh remainder bhi $3 \times 17 = 51$ hona chahiye tha, par 5 aa raha hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Agar theoretical remainder 51 hai aur actual 5, matlab inka difference $(51 - 5) = 46$ divisor $D$ se cut gaya (multiple hai).
Since initial remainder 17 tha, toh rules ke according $D > 17$ hoga.
$46$ ke factors hain 23, 46. So $D$ is purely $23$ or $46$.
Ab $4N$ par aate hain, remainder should be $4 \times 17 = 68$.
Agar usko $D$ se divide kare (let's say 23), toh $68 = 23 \times 2 + 22$. Remainder hamesha 22 aayega. Mast concept!

Future Exam Takeaway: Theoretical remainder minus actual remainder is always a multiple of the divisor. Ek baar Divisor nikal gaya toh koi bhi multiple poch le.

questions.q: Find the number of factors of $N = 2^8 \times 3^5 \times 5^4$ which are perfect cubes.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Perfect cube matlab powers ka multiple of 3 hona zaroori hai. (jaise 0, 3, 6, 9\dots).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Check ki kin powers ko select kar sakte hain:
Base 2: Max power 8. Multiples of 3 available: 0, 3, 6. (3 Choices).
Base 3: Max power 5. Multiples of 3 available: 0, 3. (2 Choices).
Base 5: Max power 4. Multiples of 3 available: 0, 3. (2 Choices).
Sabko multiply kar de: Total choices = $3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12$.
Ekdum CPR jaisi smooth counting!

questions.q: What is the sum of all integer values of $n$ for which $n^2 + 19n + 92$ is a perfect square?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Quadratic Completion

Dekh bhai, jab polynomial perfect square banani ho toh 'completing the square' lagana padta hai, bina pen ruke.

Method 1 (Concept Builder to Ninja Shortcut):
Let $n^2 + 19n + 92 = k^2$. Multiply whole equation by $4$ (to remove fractions).
$4n^2 + 76n + 368 = 4k^2$. Isko complete karo: $(2n+19)^2 - 361 + 368 = 4k^2$.
$(2n+19)^2 - 4k^2 = -7 \implies (2n+19-2k)(2n+19+2k) = -7$.
Since $-7$ prime hai, factors sirf $(\pm 1, \mp 7)$ honge. Symmetric roots aate hain in cases me. Sum of all integer values unke midpoint ke double pe settle hoti hai. Solving gives roots $n = -8, -11$. Sum is $-19$.

Ninja Hack: Aise format $n^2 + bn + c$ me sum of valid integer values humesha $-b$ ke barabar hota hai agar discriminant allow kare! Yaha $b=19$, toh sum seedha $-19$ aayega. Pen chhod de!

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Sum of all integers for a quadratic perfect square' puche toh $-b$ ka mental hack yaad rakhna, exam me $1$ minute save karega.

questions.q: If the 10-digit number $5432y1749x$ is divisible by $72$, what is the minimum possible value of $(5x - 4y)$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Base Divisibility Balancing)

Dekh bhai, $72$ ka direct divisibility rule nahi hota, humesha isko co-primes $8$ aur $9$ mein todna hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Step 1: Rule of $8$ for last 3 digits. $49x$ must be divisible by $8$. $8 \times 60 = 480$, agla multiple $488$, fir $496$. Toh seedha $x = 6$ locked.
Step 2: Rule of $9$ for sum of digits. Sum = $5+4+3+2+y+1+7+4+9+6 = 41 + y$.
Sum must be multiple of $9$. $41$ ke baad $45$ aata hai. So $41 + y = 45 \implies y = 4$.
Dono variables mil gaye. Final calculation: $5(6) - 4(4) = 30 - 16 = 14$.

Future Exam Takeaway: $72, 88, 99$ jaise bade divisors me JSM ki tarah do alag divisibility parts ko balance karte hain. Humesha end digits (jaise 8) se start karo, fir sum of digits (jaise 9 ya 11) par aao.

questions.q: What is the value of $1006^2 - 1007 \times 1005 + 1008 \times 1004 - 1009 \times 1003$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $6$

Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Saare numbers strictly $1006$ ke ird-gird set hain. Isme algebra ghusaa, number calculate karega toh barbaad ho jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Beech waale ko $x$ maan le aur baakiyo ko $(x+1), (x-1)$ form me rakh de. Terms ekdum cancel out ho jayengi.

Mathematically :-

$$ x^2 - (x+1)(x-1) + (x+2)(x-2) - (x+3)(x-3) \\ x^2 - (x^2 - 1) + (x^2 - 4) - (x^2 - 9) \\ 1 - 4 + 9 = 6 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Yahan par direct difference of squares wali basic identity ka application chal raha hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ (a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2 \\ 1006^2 - (1006^2 - 1^2) + (1006^2 - 2^2) - (1006^2 - 3^2) \\ 1 - 4 + 9 = 6 $$

TCS Trap: Exam pressure me tu in bade numbers ki unit digit nikalne ki koshish karega jisme minus sign error ke chances bohot rehte hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Never multiply! Treat consecutive massive numbers uniformly as $(x-a)(x+a)$ forms.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the number $8888\dots$ (written $25$ times) is divided by $13$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Cycle Division)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... repdigits hamesha fixed cycle me cut hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: $7, 11$, aur $13$ ka combined divisibility rule ek specific pattern create karta hai. Koi bhi ek digit ka number jab $6$ baar likha jaye ($aaaaaa$), wo $13$ se completely divide hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total $25$ digits hain. $6-6$ ki cycle me unhe uda de. $\frac{25}{6}$ ka remainder aayega $1$.
Matlab shuruwaat ke $24$ digits ($4$ pairs of $6$) mil kar perfectly zero remainder denge.
Bachega sirf aur sirf last ka aakhri $8$. Ab us akela $8$ ko $13$ se bhag dega toh remainder $8$ hi bachega.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $6$ times same digit is always divisible by $7, 11, 13, 37, 1001$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Repdigit questions ($7777\dots$) dekhte hi total digits ko $6$ se divide karke cycle choti kar lo.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $7^{84}$ is divided by 342.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Remainder theorem ka classic format! Hamesha base ki power ko aisi limit tak expand karo ki wo divisor ke aas-paas ($+1$ ya $-1$) gap me fit ho jaye. Divisor 342 hai aur Base 7, connection dikh raha hai 343 wala!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Humein pata hai $7^3 = 343$. Boom! Connection set hai.
Ab given power ko break karo: $7^{84} = (7^3)^{28}$.
Expression ban gaya $(343)^{28} \div 342$.
Ab 343 ko 342 se bhag doge toh $+1$ remainder aayega. $1^{28} = 1$. Khatam kaam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
By Binomial Expansion Remainder Theorem: $(ax + 1)^n \div ax$ always leaves a remainder of $1^n = 1$. Here $x = 1, a = 342$. $(342 + 1)^{28} \implies R = 1$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Power divisibility sawalon me humesha Dividend ko $\text{Divisor} \pm 1$ ke format me express karne ki koshish karo.

questions.q: What is the largest 4-digit number that is exactly divisible by $88$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Largest condition and $88$ divisibility criteria (yani rule 11 aur 8 check). Top se sabse bada number scan kar option list me.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Options largest to smallest line lagao. Pehle 8 aur 11 ka rule check kar direct reject condition udate ja.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Largest } 9988 \implies \frac{988}{8} \text{ fails} \\ 9966 \implies \frac{966}{8} \text{ fails} \\ 9944 \implies \frac{944}{8} = 118. \text{ And } 11 \text{ checks } (13 - 13 = 0). \\ \text{Answer fixed } = 9944 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Arithmetic absolute LCM remainder limit test apply karna traditional way me.

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{9999}{88} \implies \text{Quotient } 113, \text{ Remainder } 55 \\ 9999 - 55 = 9944 $$

TCS Trap: Traditional minus karoge toh Remainder me galati aana boht aam hai and $9900$ wagera match limit set hote hain errors me.

Exam Takeaway:

> Jab "Largest/Smallest Divisible Array Number" question complete options ke sath ho, Reverse Top Down test options ka 10x fast execution hai.

questions.q: Find the remainder when a 50-digit number formed by writing $123456789101112\dots$ is divided by $16$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Digit Counting)

Dekh bhai... aise sawalon mein pura number nahi likhna hota, sirf aakhiri tak jump karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 16 se check karna hai, so only last 4 digits matter. Hume 50th digit locate karni hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Pehle 9 numbers mein 9 digits cover ho gaye. Bachi $50 - 9 = 41$ digits.
Ab sab 2-digit numbers hain ($10, 11, \dots$). 41 digits matlab 20 pure numbers aur ek single digit ($41/2 = 20$ remainder 1).
10 se shuru karke 20 numbers $29$ tak aayenge. Agla number 30 hona tha par ek hi digit leni hai, so sirf '3'.
String ends at $28293$. 16 se last 4 digits: $8293 \pmod{16} = 5$. Khatam!

Future Exam Takeaway: Jump to the end of the series using digit block counts (1-9, 10-99) instead of writing it out sequentially.

questions.q: Determine the last three digits of $9^{100}$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Binomial Expansion)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Last 3 digits matlab calculation mod 1000 ki karni hai. Jab base 10 ke aas paas ho toh Binomial Theorem zindabad.

Pen-Free Observation: $9^{100} = (10 - 1)^{100}$. Expansion mein aakhiri 3 terms hi bachenge, baki sab 1000 se multiply hoke end mein $000$ denge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Expand karega toh aakhiri terms hongi: $\dots - \binom{100}{97} 10^3 + \binom{100}{98} 10^2 - \binom{100}{99} 10 + 1$.
Modulo 1000 karna hai, so higher powers cancel. Third last term $4950 \times 100 = 495000 \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}$.
Second last $-1000 \equiv 0$.
Aakhiri bacha sirf $+1$. So last 3 digits lock ho gaye $001$ par.

Future Exam Takeaway: For last 3 digits, shift the base to $\pm 1$ of a power of 10 and expand binomially. Most terms become zero instantly.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $4^{100}$ is divided by 6.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Ye remainder theorem ka universal truth hai bhai! 4 aur 6 ka combination jab bhi dekho, bina pen uthaye result mark kar dena.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Pattern observe kar:
$4^1 \div 6 \implies R = 4$.
$4^2 \div 6 \implies 16 \div 6 \implies R = 4$.
$4^3 \div 6 \implies 64 \div 6 \implies R = 4$.
Bhai 4 ki power chahe 100 ho ya 1 lakh, usko jab bhi 6 se bhag doge, remainder HAMESHA 4 hi aayega. Isko ratt le, seconds me answer nikalega!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Technically, $4^n = (6 - 2)^n$. This eventually boils down to checking $(-2)^n \pmod 6$, and cyclic remainders for $2^{even}$ over 6 also reduce down to pattern logic. But direct memorization is the key here.

Future Exam Takeaway: Special combinations like $4^n \div 6 \implies 4$ and $10^n \div 6 \implies 4$ fixed patterns hain, inme calculation penalty hoti hai.

questions.q: Find the total number of factors of $(73^3 - 40^3 - 33^3)$.
questions.s:
Final Output: $192$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Ye number system ka sawal hi nahi hai. Dhyan se dekh, in numbers ka seedha sum zero ban raha hai. Seedha algebra lapet isme.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Agar $a+b+c = 0$ hai toh cubes ki value $3abc$ me todi jaati hai. Waha se seedha primes ki exponents extract kar.

Mathematically :-

$$ 73 - 40 - 33 = 0 \implies 3(73)(-40)(-33) \\ \text{Take abs val: } 3 \times 73 \times 40 \times 33 \\ 3^2 \times 5^1 \times 11^1 \times 73^1 \times 2^3 \\ \text{Factors} = (3)(2)(2)(2)(4) = 192 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraic conditional identities bohot rarely par brutal tarike se test hoti hain idhar.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{If } x+y+z = 0, \text{ then } x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 3xyz \\ 3(73^1)(2^3 \times 5^1)(3^1 \times 11^1) $$

TCS Trap: Ye identity mind me nahi aayi toh tum in bade numbers ka cube nikalne chale jaoge jo practically impossible hai exam me.

Exam Takeaway:

> Sum of base terms zero ho to direct $3abc$ identity me tod do calculation fat-se banegi.

questions.q: Find the sum of the reciprocals of all the factors of $360$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Reciprocal Symmetry)

Dekh bhai, yahan sab factors likh kar fraction add karega toh agla attempt dena padega. Direct trick lagani hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique Formula):
Sum of Reciprocals of Factors = $\frac{\text{Sum of Factors}}{N}$.
Pehle $360$ ka prime factorization kar: $360 = 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5^1$.
Sum of factors formula: $\frac{2^4-1}{2-1} \times \frac{3^3-1}{3-1} \times \frac{5^2-1}{5-1}$
$= 15 \times 13 \times 6 = 1170$.
Ab seedha value daal: $\frac{1170}{360} = \frac{117}{36} = \frac{13}{4} = 3.25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Sum of reciprocals ka ek universal shortcut $\frac{\text{Sum of Divisors}}{N}$ apni notes me bold karke likh lo.

questions.q: If a 10-digit number $2094x843y2$, is divisible by 88, for the maximum possible value of x the value of (5x-7y) is?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Base Divisibility Balancing)

Dekh bhai... 88 jaisi badi values composite hoti hain. Inhe 8 aur 11 mein tod ke constraints satisfy karo.

Pen-Free Observation: Hamesha last 3 digits rule (8) pehle lagao taaki 'y' ki limited values mil jayein.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
88 matlab 8 aur 11.
Div by 8: last 3 digits $3y2$ chahiye. $y=1$ (312), $y=5$ (352), $y=9$ (392) satisfy karenge.
Ab 11 ka alternate sum: $(15+x+y) - 17 = x+y-2$. Yeh $0$ ya $11$ hona chahiye.
Max $x$ ke liye $x+y-2=11 \implies x+y=13$. Agar hum $y=5$ lenge toh $x=8$ perfectly set hota hai.
Equation mein dal: $5(8) - 7(5) = 40 - 35 = 5$. Question tod diya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Always find all possibilities for the unit digit from the $2^n$ rule before blindly applying the alternate sum 11's rule.

questions.q: When two numbers are separately divided by $44$ the remainders are $11$ and $38$ respectively. If the sum of the two number is divided by $44$, then the obtained remainder will be?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Remainder Addition)

Dekh bhai, remainder theorem ka universal law hai: Jo numbers ka operation bola hai, wahi unke remainders ka kardo.

Pen-Free Observation: Dono case mein divisor $44$ hai. Final divisor bhi $44$ hai. Seedha remainders add kar do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Naye number ka base banega $11 + 38 = 49$.
Ab directly $49$ ko $44$ se divide kar de. $49 \pmod{44}$ seedha remainder $5$ dega. Pen rakh do!

Future Exam Takeaway: Add, Subtract ya multiply, jo operation numbers ke saath likha ho woh hamesha base remainders par utar diya karo. Constants maintain rehte hain.

questions.q: What are the last three digits of $11^{2020}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Last 3 digits nikalne ka matlab hai 1000 se remainder dhoondhna. Base 11 ko 10+1 likh sakte hain, so Binomial expansion hi single way out hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Binomial approach laga bhai: $11^{2020} = (10 + 1)^{2020}$.
Expand karega toh pehli saari terms me 10 ki power 3 ya usse badi hogi (yaani sab 1000 se cut jayenge end me 000 aayega). Sirf aakhiri do terms matters karengi!
Second last term: $\binom{2020}{1} \times 10^1 \times 1^{2019} = 2020 \times 10 = 20200$. Yahan se end ke 3 digit aaye $200$.
Last term: $1^{2020} = 1$.
Toh total $200 + 1 = 201$. Option ud gaya!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
$(x+a)^n$ expansion mein last $k$ digits nikalne ke liye last $k$ terms ko observe karna hota hai jab $x$ 10, 100 type ka multiple ho.

Future Exam Takeaway: End digits poochne par number ko powers of 10 ke nearest binomial format ($10^k \pm 1$) mein break kardo.

questions.q: If a book has $250$ pages, how many digits have been used to number the pages.
questions.s:
Final Output: $642$

Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Pagination me fix milestones set hain pehle se. Ye question seedha formula blocks ka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Pehle 99 pages ki constant value $189$ yaad rakh. Uske baad jo bhi 3-digit pages bache hain usme $3$ multiply maar kar add kar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Pages } 1 \text{ to } 99 \implies 189 \text{ digits} \\ \text{Remaining 3-digit pages} = 250 - 99 = 151 \\ \text{Total} = 189 + (151 \times 3) = 642 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Range break kar ke step by step addition chal raha hai yahan. 1-digit wale $9$, 2-digit wale $90$, bache 3-digit wale.

Mathematically :-

$$ (9 \times 1) + (90 \times 2) + (151 \times 3) \\ 9 + 180 + 453 = 642 $$

TCS Trap: 3-digit pages nikalne ke chakkar me log directly $250-100 = 150$ kar dete hain, jabki count me 100th page bhi included hota hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Standard pagination facts yaad rakh: 1 se 99 pages me exactly 189 digits hoti hain, aur 1 se 999 me 2889 digits.

questions.q: Find the greatest value of $b$ so that $30a68b$ (where $a > b$) is divisible by 11.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
11 ki divisibility means alternate digits sum ka difference 0, 11, 22 hona chahiye. $a>b$ ka constraint dhyan rakhna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $30a68b$ me sums nikal:
$S_1 = 3+a+8 = 11+a$
$S_2 = 0+6+b = 6+b$
Difference = $5+a-b$.
Difference 0 nahi ho sakta kyuki $a>b$ (positive result aayega). Toh isko 11 ke barabar rakh: $5+a-b = 11 \implies a-b = 6$.
$b$ ki maximum value chahiye, toh $a$ ko maximum single digit 9 rakh. $b = 9-6 = 3$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Basic equations se constraints dhyan na rakhne pe marks kat-te hain. $a$ aur $b$ dono digits hain (0-9).

Future Exam Takeaway:
Jab bhi do unknowns $a, b$ hon aur maximum/minimum pucha jaye, ek ko 9 ya 0 boundary value dekar dusre ko set kiya kar.
